sources.name: Exchange terms of service / restricted jurisdictions pages
sources.note: Compliance filtering is conservative and simplified; users must verify eligibility themselves. KuCoin: barred to US residents by SDNY court order (Jan 2025, CFTC order Mar 2026); KuCoin terms also restrict mainland China, Hong Kong, Singapore and Thailand (mandatory KYC enforced 2026). Kraken: mainland China not served; Kraken states it is not licensed/regulated in Singapore under the post-2025-06 DTSP regime (MAS), so SG residents are excluded; spot serves US (state-level limits apply, e.g. historical NY restrictions) and Kraken/Bitnomial CFTC-regulated perpetuals rolled out to 47 US states in Jun 2026; Hong Kong residents can onboard with HKID via the offshore platform; Japan (JFSA), Canada, UK, EU (MiCA) and Australia are served.

sources.name: Coinbase availability by jurisdiction (2026 audits)
sources.note: Coinbase serves all 50 US states and holds a Singapore MAS MPI licence (DPT + cross-border transfer, since 2023-10). Mainland China: not served (domestic crypto ban). Hong Kong: retail service unavailable (withdrew its VASP licence application in 2023 and has not returned). Japan: entity retains FSA registration but no active retail service since the 2023 wind-down (conflicting reports; conservatively modeled as blocked). Thailand: no Thai SEC licence / availability evidence (conservatively modeled as blocked).

sources.name: Hyperliquid regional access (ToS restricted list + 2026 reports)
sources.note: No KYC (wallet = identity). United States: front-end geo-blocked and ToS lists US persons as restricted (VPN circumvention prohibited); on-chain protocol remains reachable — modeled as blocked. Canada: restricted only in Ontario per ToS (modeled as allowed). UK: accessible but added to the FCA unauthorized-firm consumer warning list 2026-05-21 (modeled as allowed, caveat only). Restricted elsewhere: Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria, Crimea/DNR/LNR regions. Mainland China/HK/SG/JP/TH: not front-end blocked (local law still applies). Third-party 2026 audits: datawallet 2026-04-28, kurslog 2026-06-06, financefeeds 2026-08-20.

sources.name: BingX Customer Agreement restricted jurisdictions (agreement dated 2026-09-02, Nieve Cruz Cruz PA Corporation) + datawallet regional audit 2026-07-16
sources.note: Modeled as blocked: United States (all territories), Canada, United Kingdom, mainland China, Hong Kong, Singapore, Netherlands, Macau, sanctioned jurisdictions (Cuba/Iran/North Korea/Afghanistan/Myanmar/Somalia/Burundi/CAR/DRC), Crimea/DNR/LNR, plus Cambodia/Laos/Panama. Japan, Thailand (BingX's #1 traffic source), Australia, Vietnam, Kazakhstan, Ukraine and 160+ other countries are served outside the EEA. v0.41: no MiCA CASP authorization (Austria FMA application pending/unapproved), so BingX is blocked across ALL 30 EEA states via region_blocked — the former NL-only key is subsumed; MO/KH/LA/PA restrictions are not otherwise modeled.

sources.name: Phemex restricted jurisdictions (rononcrypto Phemex Review 2026 + decentralised.news Phemex vs BingX 2026 + TradersUnion availability list, verified 2026-09-12)
sources.note: Phemex (Singapore) is explicitly blocked in the United States and United Kingdom. Conservatively modeled as also blocked in Canada and Hong Kong (decentralised.news lists these as restricted; some regional audits show partial availability — users must verify). EU/EEA: no MiCA CASP authorization and fiat already blocked in NL/PL; v0.41 blocks the entire EEA via region_blocked after the 2026-07-01 cliff. Served in most of Asia (incl. SG/JP/TH), LatAm, Africa and the Middle East.

sources.name: BloFin Terms of Use §6 Restricted Locations (revised 2026-07-03, 43 jurisdictions) + datawallet regional audit 2026-08-12 + ESMA MiCA transitional-period statement (cliff 2026-07-01)
sources.note: Modeled as blocked: United States (all states/territories), Canada, mainland China, Singapore (plus India/UAE and ~35 sanctions/FATF jurisdictions not otherwise keyed here). Served (not on the Restricted list): Hong Kong, Japan, Thailand, United Kingdom, Brazil, Australia, Turkey, Korea and 150+ other countries; optional KYC with a 20,000 USDT no-KYC daily withdrawal cap. EU/EEA: BloFin holds NO MiCA CASP authorization and is not in the ESMA register — since the 2026-07-01 grandfathering cliff it has no legal basis to serve EEA residents; v0.41 enforces this EEA-wide via region_blocked (blofin => [EEA]) instead of the former Germany-only key. No direct fiat rails (third-party card/SEPA widgets only).

sources.name: Bitstamp jurisdictional footprint (official licensing + 2026 regional audits, incl. exchangeselector.com country pages 2026-08)
sources.note: Founded 2011 (Luxembourg), acquired by Robinhood 2025-06-02; serves 5M+ users under a multi-jurisdiction stack: EU/EEA via Bitstamp Europe S.A. CSSF MiCA CASP authorization (2025-05-16) with full passporting; US via Bitstamp USA (NYDFS BitLicense + FinCEN MSB + state MTLs); UK FCA registration (978690); Canada FINTRAC; Singapore MAS Major Payment Institution; Japan service via the BVI/APAC entities. Mainland China and standard sanctions/FATF jurisdictions are not served (modeled venue-blocked in CN). PRODUCT GATING: regulated perpetual futures (live 2026-04 via the MiFID-authorized Slovenian entity, CSSF passport) are offered to ELIGIBLE EEA RESIDENTS ONLY. v0.40 models this as a POSITIVE allowlist (product_region_gates.bitstamp.futures = [EEA], regions.EEA = EU27 + IS/LI/NO, 30 states) instead of the v0.38 negative list: any supplied country outside the EEA (US/CA/GB/JP/SG/HK/TH/AU/BR/CH/TR/KR/...) is blocked for futures; GB retail access is also closed under the FCA 2021 crypto-derivatives ban and Switzerland is not inside the MiCA/EEA passport. Spot remains available in every non-blocked jurisdiction. Users must still verify their own residency eligibility.

sources.name: Bitvavo jurisdictional footprint (AFM CASP register + MiCA passporting; regional audits verified 2026-09-13: cryptowinrate restricted-jurisdictions list, CoinMarketCap exchange profile, Apple App Store UK approval record)
sources.note: Bitvavo B.V. (Amsterdam, Netherlands) holds AFM MiCA CASP authorization #41000010 (granted 2025-06-27) and passports into all 30 EEA states; it is the largest EU-native exchange by euro spot volume. v0.42 models its service area with a POSITIVE venue allowlist region_allowed.bitvavo = [EEA]: it does not onboard residents of the United States, Canada, Japan, Singapore, Brazil, Australia, mainland China or most other modeled countries (its restricted-jurisdictions list also covers sanctions/FATF states). UK and CH access exists via separately licensed arrangements (UK service runs through Gateway 21 Limited, FCA-framework entity, approved on the UK App Store 2026-08-10; Switzerland reports conflict between CMC and third-party restricted lists) — conservatively NOT modeled as available in GB/CH pending entity-level verification; users must verify residency eligibility themselves. Spot only: no exchange-hosted perpetuals/futures (margin up to 10x exists but is not modeled).

sources.name: Finst jurisdictional footprint (AFM register + official/legal pages; verified 2026-09-13: finst.com/en/company, finst.com/en/security, exchangeselector.com review updated 2026-07-08)
sources.note: Finst B.V. (Amsterdam, KvK 85668117, founded 2022 by ex-DEGIRO managers) holds AFM MiCA CASP authorization #41000015 (granted July 2025) passported across the EEA — Finst states it serves 30 European countries / 110K+ retail and institutional investors; one independent profile counts 28 countries. v0.43 models its service area with the POSITIVE venue allowlist region_allowed.finst = [EEA]: the United States, United Kingdom, Switzerland, Canada, Japan, Singapore, Brazil, Australia, mainland China and other non-EEA residents are not onboarded (TradersUnion availability page confirms US not served). SPOT/BROKERAGE ONLY: no margin, leverage, futures or derivatives of any kind (classifies unsupported_product, not region-blocked, for futures queries inside the EEA). Bank-transfer-only funding (iDEAL/Bancontact/SEPA). Users must verify residency eligibility themselves.

sources.name: Bitpanda jurisdictional footprint (BaFin/FMA register entries, FCA UK register, FMA penalty notice, coinspeaker/kagels-trading regional coverage; verified 2026-09-13)
sources.note: Bitpanda GmbH (Vienna, founded 2014; ~7.4M users end-2025) is the most broadly licensed modeled venue: BaFin granted MiCA CASP authorization on 2025-01-27 (passported into all 30 EEA states) and the Austrian FMA granted its own authorization on 2025-04; the FMA's €70,000 fine of 2026-08-14 concerned whitepaper-timing/marketing formalities (first published Austrian MiCA penalty) and did not restrict the licence. UK residents are served through Bitpanda Broker UK Ltd (registered FCA cryptoasset business; GBP Faster Payments, £10 minimum fiat deposit). v0.44 models the service area as region_allowed.bitpanda = [EEA, GB] (GB represented as its own one-member region key): US, CA, CN, IN, RU and other non-EEA/non-GB residents are not onboarded; the lighter crypto-only availability reported in AU/JP/SG/BR/MX/TR/CH is conservatively NOT modeled pending entity-level verification. SPOT/BROKERAGE ONLY: no exchange-hosted futures or perpetuals (unsupported_product inside the service area); margin up to 10x exists but is not modeled. Users must verify residency eligibility themselves.

sources.name: BISON jurisdictional footprint (official BISON support 'In welchen Ländern ist BISON verfügbar?', BISON press kits 2025-09/2026-01, ESMA MiCA register entries for BSDC/EUWAX; verified 2026-09-13)
sources.note: BISON (Boerse Stuttgart Group, Stuttgart; app operated by Sowa Labs GmbH, trading counterparty EUWAX AG) is ACTIVELY offered for crypto trading in Germany, Austria and Switzerland, and accepts individuals from 72 nationalities who are resident and domiciled in an EEA Agreement contracting state (EU27+IS/LI/NO) or in Switzerland via passive freedom to provide services; securities trading is Germany-only. v0.45 models the service area with the POSITIVE venue allowlist region_allowed.bison = [EEA, CH] (CH represented as its own one-member region key, same pattern as GB for Bitpanda): US, GB, CA, JP, SG, AU, BR, CN and other non-EEA/non-CH residents are not onboarded. Licensing: Boerse Stuttgart Digital Custody GmbH (formerly blocknox) = FIRST BaFin MiCAR licensee (custody/transfer 2025-01-17, 29-state passport); EUWAX AG = BaFin MiCAR exchange services 2025-04-01 (8-state passport) plus order execution 2025-11-21 (Germany only). SPOT/BROKERAGE ONLY: no futures or margin (unsupported_product inside the service area). Users must verify residency eligibility themselves.

sources.name: Post-MiCA-cliff EEA availability sweep (ESMA statement 2026-04-17; ESMA interim CASP register sync 2026-09-11 via citiumtech.com/resources/mica-crypto-registry/major-exchanges; blockzeit MiCA tracker; Bloomberg via laicrypto 2026-09-04; Finance Magnates MiCA Day One test 2026-07-01; kagels-trading.de FMA status 2026-09-06; bitcoinmarket.net EU day-trading audit 2026-07-07)
sources.note: The MiCA Article 143(3) grandfathering period ended 2026-07-01 with NO extension: serving EEA residents without CASP authorization breaches EU law (fines up to EUR 15M or 12.5% turnover). v0.41 models this with region_blocked at VENUE level for all 30 EEA states: BINANCE (withdrew Greek HCMC application 2026-06-24 over fit-and-proper grounds; halted new sign-ups/spot orders/deposits/margin/futures/Earn for FR/IT/ES/PL/SE/LT from 2026-07-01, ~2M French users; withdrawals stay open; some residual service via contested reverse-solicitation/Abu-Dhabi routing under ESMA scrutiny — modeled blocked, the conservative legal status), MEXC (no CASP; flagged unlicensed by Dutch AFM; told EU users to withdraw before the cliff), BITGET (no CASP; Austria FMA application pending; France fully suspended since 2026-03-31; states it will not serve EEA without authorization), BLOFIN (no CASP, not in ESMA register), PHEMEX (no CASP; fiat already blocked in NL/PL; standing rests on tolerance, not licence), BINGX (Austria FMA application at advanced stage but NOT approved as of 2026-09), KUCOIN (CASP authorized via FMA Austria 2025-11-27 but the FMA commencement-of-business prohibition of 2026-02-18 remains in force as of 2026-09-06 after AML-officer gaps; EU trading/deposits halted 2026-02-04, no new EEA accounts — modeled blocked for new business; legacy customers retain limited service). CASP-AUTHORIZED and open for spot in the EEA: okx (Malta MFSA, 9/10 service codes), gate (Gate Technology Ltd, Malta MFSA), bybit (Bybit EU GmbH, Austria FMA — spot + margin capped 10x via bybit.eu), kraken (Ireland CBI), coinbase (Luxembourg CSSF), bitstamp (Luxembourg CSSF). HYPERLIQUID is a non-custodial perp DEX: NOT CASP-authorized and on EU regulators' watch lists, but its front-end does not geo-block EEA users (deposits/perps verified working from IT/AT without ID, ToS restrict only US/Ontario/sanctioned) — left AVAILABLE with an explicit unauthorized-provider risk note because accessibility is factual and pure DeFi sits in an unresolved MiCA grey zone ahead of MiCA 2.0. PRODUCT-LEVEL (product_region_blocked): crypto derivatives/perpetuals require a SEPARATE MiFID II investment-firm licence (ESMA 2026-02-24: perps are likely CFDs; OKX launched X-Perps as 5-year-dated futures 2026-04). As of 2026-09 the only modeled venues with live EEA-authorized perps are OKX (MiFID entity, X-Perps), KRAKEN (CySEC MiFID acquisition, 10x cap) and BITSTAMP (Slovenian MiFID entity, live 2026-04); BYBIT's Bybit X GmbH MiFID II application (filed 2025-09) was still unapproved as of 2026-07-07 and GATE has no live EEA derivatives entity, so both are futures-blocked across the EEA while spot stays open. Non-EEA countries are unaffected by these gates.
